algorithm.title: Evaluation of fever in infants up to 60 days of age

cell.label: Evaluation of fever in infants up to 60 days of age. Focal infection?
Well appearing (interactive, good perfusion, no respiratory distress or lethargy)?

Order lab studies: CBC, blood culture; UA and urine culture (catheterized or suprapubic tap). If not low risk (see Table 1), consider CSF culture and CSF studies. Additional studies if applicable: if tachypnea, CXR; if diarrhea, stool smear and culture.
CSF pleocytosis? If CSF not obtained, is the infant <29 days?
Secure follow-up within 12-24 hours (family and physician agreement)?

Obtain routine laboratory studies: complete blood count (CBC), blood culture; urinalysis (UA) and urine culture (catheterized or suprapubic tap); cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) culture and CSF studies (cell count, glucose, protein). Additional studies if applicable: if tachypnea, chest x-ray (CXR); if diarrhea, stool smear and culture. Give empiric antibiotics (Table 2). Hospitalize and observe until cultures remain negative for 24-36 hours. Consider herpes simplex virus for infants <28 days.
Give empiric antibiotics (Table 2) and hospitalize until cultures are negative for 24-36 hours.
Two options: (1) give IV/IM antibiotics (see Table 2) and observe at home, reassessing in 24 hours; or (2) give IV/IM antibiotics (see Table 2) and observe in the hospital.
Manage according to laboratory results, study results, and clinical course.
